items.stem:
Nandini kept reading about farmers who lose crops for lack of cold storage. After weeks of study, the idea of a solar-powered cold box came to her suddenly one morning. She built a model, tested it on two farms and improved it. Later she sold the boxes on rent to farmers at ₹50 a day.
(i) Identify the stages of the creative process in the case. (ii) Identify one product and one marketing innovation.
items.answer: (i) Preparation (reading and study); incubation (weeks of working on it); illumination (idea came suddenly); verification (built a model, tested and improved). (ii) Product – solar-powered cold box; marketing – renting the boxes at ₹50 a day.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Preparation (reading and study); incubation (weeks of working on it); illumination (idea came suddenly); verification (built a model, tested and improved). (ii) Product – solar-powered cold box; marketing – renting the boxes at ₹50 a day.

items.stem:
Students in Ranchi wanted to help street vendors who lose vegetables in the heat. They spent days with vendors, wrote down the problem as "vendors need a cheap way to keep vegetables fresh for a day without electricity", listed many ideas, built a clay-and-sand cooling box from waste material and tried it with five vendors, who suggested a larger lid.
(i) Identify the five stages of design thinking in the case. (ii) Why is the problem statement important?
items.answer: (i) Empathise (spent days with vendors); define (wrote the problem statement); ideate (listed many ideas); prototype (built the clay-and-sand box); test (tried with five vendors and got feedback). (ii) It keeps the solution focused on the user's real need.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Empathise (spent days with vendors); define (wrote the problem statement); ideate (listed many ideas); prototype (built the clay-and-sand box); test (tried with five vendors and got feedback). (ii) It keeps the solution focused on the user's real need.

items.stem: Explain any five benefits of design thinking for an entrepreneur.
items.answer: (i) Focus on real needs: Solutions are based on what users actually need. (ii) Lower cost of failure: Cheap prototypes reveal problems early. (iii) Encourages creativity: Many ideas are explored before choosing. (iv) Better customer acceptance: Users help shape the product. (v) Continuous improvement: Testing and feedback keep improving the solution.
items.markingKey: Any five points, 1 mark each (point with a line of explanation): (i) Focus on real needs: Solutions are based on what users actually need. (ii) Lower cost of failure: Cheap prototypes reveal problems early. (iii) Encourages creativity: Many ideas are explored before choosing. (iv) Better customer acceptance: Users help shape the product. (v) Continuous improvement: Testing and feedback keep improving the solution.

items.stem:
